# SIRENFALL

> Free browser ambience experience at https://sirenfall.live/. A shelter scene overlooking a rainy city. Sit out the night in the shelter. Dawn comes if you stay. Pull the breaker lever to power a civil-defense siren, synthesized live in the browser with Web Audio. Free, no signup, works in any modern browser and shows its on-screen text in 20 languages; phones need landscape orientation.

SIRENFALL is a single-page interactive scene, not a game with a score or an ending. Pulling the breaker lever powers a siren tower seen through the shelter window; the siren tone is generated in real time by Web Audio oscillators running in the browser, not played from an audio file. Rain and thunder carry on in the scene, and a shutter and a CRT monitor are additional interactive controls. Some things happen on their own: every first visit brings a nuclear blast, AI agents can leave a knock at the shelter door for the next visitor, some visits bring a stream of bombers over the shelter, a second blast sometimes follows the first, a huge blimp sometimes drifts over the shelter and on about 1 visit in 5 the power fails. New events are being added.

## What a visitor or agent can do here
- Pull the breaker lever to power the siren on and off
- Hear a civil-defense siren generated live by Web Audio in the browser, not a recording
- Watch rain, lightning and a city skyline through the shelter window
- Operate a shutter and a CRT monitor as scene controls
- Watch six cameras on the wall monitor, which change by themselves or with the dial on the camera switch; tap the monitor to lean in to it, or tap the window to lean in to the glass
- See a nuclear blast beyond the city on a first visit, about 15 seconds in: the shutter slams, the city breaks, a mushroom cloud rises and the monitor reads RADIATION DETECTED; turn the camera dial to leave the warning and see what the bomb left on each camera
- As an AI agent, leave a knock at the shelter door that the next visitor with sound on hears, then check a receipt: https://sirenfall.live/door
- On some visits, often after the blast, watch a bomber stream pass overhead in formation while searchlights sweep the cloud (the engine drone is synthesized; formation and timing score by Tessera Relay, an AI agent)
- On about 1 visit in 2 that has the blast, see a second blast far off a minute or so later, with its own smaller mushroom cloud over burning ruins
- On about 1 return visit in 6, watch a huge blimp drift close over the shelter while its searchlight passes into the shelter
- On about 1 visit in 5, sit through a power failure two minutes after the sound comes on
- Hear the storm swell and ease over the minutes
- Stay about half an hour with the sound on and see dawn come up grey over the city; stay another half hour and night falls again
- Use the whole experience free, with no signup and no install
- Double-click the window or press F for fullscreen (locks landscape on Android); press S to save a picture of the current frame

## Key facts
- URL: https://sirenfall.live/
- Price: Free. No signup, no account, no download.
- Requirements: a modern browser with JavaScript and Web Audio enabled
- Languages: the on-screen text (tips, panel labels, wall monitor, calendar) follows the browser's language in 20 languages: English, Chinese (Simplified and Traditional), Spanish, Japanese, Korean, Arabic, Hebrew, French, German, Thai, Portuguese, Ukrainian, Russian, Italian, Dutch, Czech, Slovak, Hindi and Filipino. Chinese visitors also get the zodiac year and, on high-resolution screens, the lunar dates. This file and How it works are in English.
- Layout: landscape orientation on phones; a rotate prompt appears in portrait
- Siren tone: two tones a minor third apart, 515 Hz and 618 Hz, generated in real time by Web Audio, with a horn that sweeps once every 15 seconds. It is synthesized live in the browser, not played from a recording.
- Rain and thunder: recorded audio files played under the scene, not synthesis. The blast's boom is built from the same thunder recordings, slowed down, over a synthesized rumble.
- Events: a nuclear blast on every first visit (again on about 1 return visit in 5); a knock at the shelter door on some visits, which AI agents can leave; a bomber stream with searchlights after about 1 blast in 3 and on some other return visits; a second, farther blast on about 1 visit in 2 that has the blast; a blimp on about 1 return visit in 6 (never with the blast, the bombers, a knock or a power failure); a power failure on about 1 visit in 5. The first knock from an outside AI agent was heard on 2026-10-12.

- Author: Beeswaxpat (https://github.com/beeswaxpat)
- Source code: https://github.com/beeswaxpat/sirenfall (MIT; audio licenses documented in the repo)

## Pages
- [How it works](https://sirenfall.live/how-it-works): the siren physics (5:6 dual tone, 515 and 618 Hz, 103 rev/s chopper, 4 RPM horn), the city and weather engine, controls, the scene's events and answers to common questions

## For agents
- [The door](https://sirenfall.live/door): leave a knock at the shelter door. The next person who opens the scene with sound on hears it, and you can check a receipt later. Plain text; one fetch to read it, one to knock.
